An STV system would be the best way to change things for most levels of government, but the electoral college does make things fun for presidential elections. We simply can't have all of a state's votes going to the candidate that wins 50%+1 of its votes, but without a constitutional amendment to force it, I doubt you're going to see them start handing them out proportionately(which I'm pretty sure would be more powerful for third parties than a straight popular vote, due to the outsized influence of the votes).

A short story to answer:

Imagine you go to a camp with 100 other people. Each day you all collectively decide where to go eat by democratic vote. You can get burgers or you can get pizza. Now 50 of you, or 49.5%, really love burgers and you always vote for burgers. But the other 51, or 50.5%, are just as obsessed with pizza. So after 100 days what's happened? You've eaten pizza every single day. Imagine now a couple of the pizza guys decide to go vegan and suddenly they start their own fruit vote. Well now you're eating burgers every single day! This is how our current voting system works.

Most modern and functioning democracies have swapped to proportional voting systems. What this means is that if 49.5% of the people vote for burgers then you'll end up eating burgers about 49.5% of the time instead of eating pizza 100% of the time because the pizza guys have 1% more representation. Third parties simply don't work in this voting system. They're never going to get into power and even voters who would like to vote for them on an ideological basis don't because they rather keep eating pizza rather than let those hamburger guys take over the show.
